one_sentence_story: By putting 71 Stanford students through an hour of turning 48 square wooden pegs in 1959, Leon Festinger and J. Merrill Carlsmith proved that volunteers paid just $1 to praise the dull chore came to genuinely believe it was fun (+1.35) while volunteers paid $20 stayed unimpressed (-0.05) — because insufficient external reward forces the mind to resolve Cognitive Dissonance by changing its own belief.
so_what_for_you: When coaching kids or teams toward lasting inner values, use **just enough** structure plus genuine choice rather than giant external bribes — and watch out when your own brain starts inventing glowing praise for a bad sunk-cost deal.
